name: Ciprofloxacin
executiveSummary: Fluoroquinolone. Adult PO 250–750 mg every 12 h or IV 400 mg every 8–12 h by focus; pediatrics 20–30 mg/kg/day only for special indications (osteoarticular risk).
indications:
## Indications

- Complicated UTI, pyelonephritis, skin/soft-tissue infections, osteomyelitis, GI/abdominal infections due to susceptible gram-negatives.
- Selected respiratory/otitis infections when no alternative and documented susceptibility.
- Meningococcal contact prophylaxis (single dose).

## Precautions

- Tendinopathy/tendon rupture, neuropathy, QT, photosensitivity; avoid routine use under 18 years.
- Separate from antacids, Ca/Mg/Al, sucralfate, and dairy (↓ absorption).
- Adjust in renal failure.

> Prefer alternatives in pediatrics except cystic fibrosis, pyelonephritis, or other institutional exceptions.

adulto.presentation: Tablets 250–500–750 mg; IV solution 200 mg/100 mL or 400 mg/200 mL.
adulto.dose: PO: mild–moderate **250–500 mg every 12 h**; severe/complicated **500–750 mg every 12 h**. IV: **400 mg every 12 h** (severe: **400 mg every 8 h**). Meningococcal prophylaxis: **500 mg PO once**.
adulto.administration: PO away from meals/cations. IV: no bolus; 200 mg over ~30 min, 400 mg over ~60 min. Keep light protection until use (by presentation).
adulto.notes: PO≈IV bioequivalence allows oral step-down in many infections.

pediatrico.presentation: Tablets 250–500 mg; compounded ~30 mg/mL; IV 200–400 mg; ophthalmic 0.3%.
pediatrico.dose: Mild–moderate: **20 mg/kg/day every 12 h** (max PO **500 mg/dose**; IV **400 mg/dose**). Severe / pyelonephritis / CF: **30 mg/kg/day** (PO every 12 h, max **1.5 g/day**; IV every 8 h, max **1.2 g/day**). Meningococcal prophylaxis: **20 mg/kg PO once** (max **500 mg**).
pediatrico.administration: PO/IV/topical. IV dilute to ~2 mg/mL; infuse ~60 min.
pediatrico.notes: Restricted pediatric use. ↑ nephrotoxicity with cyclosporine.

neonatal.dose: ID/NNU exceptions only; no standard neonatal fever regimen.
neonatal.notes: Osteoarticular and resistance risks; avoid unless no alternatives.

stability:
## Stability

- Ready-to-use IV: per manufacturer; protect from light until administration.
- Compounded/opened PO: typically up to 14 days at room temperature (check label).
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, rash, crystalluria, arthralgia. Serious: tendon rupture (≥ 48 h), neuropathy, hypersensitivity, *Clostridioides difficile*.
